notes.1a: The manufacturing account was prepared to a high standard with a few fully correct accounts. Some entries were placed in an incorrect section and some candidates omitted carriage inwards.
notes.1b: The income statement was also well prepared but there were fewer fully correct answers. Errors included the incorrect treatment of production cost and the incorrect calculation of the finance cost. A few candidates failed to add the factory profit and/or deduct the increase in the provision for unrealised profit.
notes.1c: Some candidates calculated the floor area correctly and there were no common incorrect answers.
notes.1d: Many candidates named the correct section.
notes.1e: The discussion was well answered with many candidates providing three valid points with the consequent award of three marks.
notes.2a: The statement of financial position was presented with a range of errors from most candidates with very few receiving half of the available marks. Very few candidates made the required impairment losses adjustment and there were relatively few correct postings for trade receivables. Many candidates did not account for the share premium and although most attempted to adjust the retained earnings there were very few fully correct postings. Very few candidates split the bank loan between non-current liabilities and current liabilities.
notes.2b: Many candidates stated correctly which event was adjusting and which was non-adjusting.
notes.2c: Few candidates were able to state a possible reason for revaluation with hardly any developing their answer to receive the second mark.
notes.2d: This was well answered with most candidates giving the required advice and many justifying their answer satisfactorily often with the use of an accounting concept.
notes.3a: This was not well answered with a high number of candidates just writing a formula.
notes.3b: This was answered to a reasonable standard with most candidates identifying the relevant ratios and some providing a very good explanation.
notes.3c: Most candidates demonstrated their knowledge of the required ratios with some fully correct answers being awarded twelve marks. The ratio which caused the most difficulty was dividend yield 9706 Accounting November 2022 and this was usually due to lack of knowledge of the formula. A limited number of candidates were penalised as they did not present their answers to two decimal places.
notes.3d: The discussion of the changes in the ratios was not well answered. Few candidates considered both the numerator and denominator of the ratios when analysing the changes and consequently the award of marks for this question was low.
notes.3e: The explanation was not well answered with few candidates providing any relevant points.
notes.4a: Although there were very few fully correct calculations most candidates did account for some of the components and were credited accordingly. A common error was the incorrect inclusion of the members transferring to life membership.
notes.4b: The subscription account was well prepared with some fully correct accounts. The most common errors were the omission of the irrecoverable debt and the reversal of the opening and/or closing balances.
notes.4c: Some candidates were able to make the life membership calculations without errors with a higher number calculating the fees for the income and expenditure account correctly.
notes.4d: A high number of candidates were able to suggest two relevant sources of income.
notes.4e: Nearly all candidates gave the required advice and the justification was invariably acceptable with some candidates receiving five marks. Weaker answers tended to repeat points.
notes.5a: Very few candidates were able to give a valid explanation with hardly any mentioning discounting.
notes.5b: The table was generally well prepared with some being fully correct and no common errors.
notes.5c: There were some correct NPV calculations but a significant number of candidates did not discount the total changes in costs and some failed to adjust their increased NPV with the existing NPV.
notes.5d: Most candidates gave the required advice along with two valid points so a common award was three marks but very few provided the extra points to receive all five available marks.
notes.5e: There were very few correct calculations and it was rare to see the revised NPV converted backwards by using the year four discount factor.
notes.5f: Most candidates demonstrated their knowledge and understanding of the internal rate of return and the explanations were generally reasonable.
notes.6a: Some candidates calculated the overhead absorption rate correctly but there were also many incorrect answers. Most candidates then accounted correctly for the direct costs but few calculated the fixed overhead cost correctly and consequently there were few correct total standard cost calculations.
notes.6b: The reconciliation statement was not well prepared with hardly any fully correct statements being submitted. Many candidates ignored the instruction to include two direct mateial, two direct labour and two fixed overhead variances and some made variance calculations without attempting the reconciliation.
notes.6c: Nearly all candidates provided the required advice but few gave more than two valid points of justification.
notes.6d: Many candidates understood the difference between a fixed and a flexed budget but fewer were able to state a reason for preparing a flexed budget.
